newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Moran results spark Orogen, Oil Search shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Moran results spark Orogen, Oil Search shares.

text.p: Shares in Oil Search Ltd and mining investor Orogen Minerals Ltd rocketed to record highs of A$2.30 and A$2.49 respectively on Wednesday, ignited by Tuesday's promising drilling results from the Moran 1X exploration well onshore Papua New Guinea.
"It was a good report," said a Sydney-based resource analyst, saying the results confirmed earlier drilling reports.
"They have hydrocarbons in two of the sections which basically repeated what they found in the original well. It's encouraging because it could be a new reservoir."
Others agreed that the report was underlying the move, although they suggested the shares may have topped out.
"That is where the interest is coming there but it's probably getting to the stage where they are a bit pricey now," said dealer Martin Angel of Eyres Reed.
By 1.00 p.m. (0200 GMT), Oil Search shares were 13 cents higher at A$2.28 on turnover of 944,971 shares while Orogen shares were 13 cents higher at A$2.39 on turnover of 4.5 million shares.
On Tuesday, Oil Search reported the Moran 1X/Sidetrack 3 well, in permit PDL-2, had encountered hydrocarbon shows and elevated formation resistivities in two separate formations.
The encounters were in a structurally repeated section of the Toro C Sandstone between 3,418 metres and 3,509 metres measured depth and in the Digimu Sandstone between 3,609 metres and 3,677 metres.
The significance of these shows will be assessed by wireline logging and repeat formation testing, Oil Search said.
